key_insight: Natural-image pretraining improved medical diffusion image generation, with benefits linked more to spatial structure than semantic understanding.
clinical_relevance: Higher-quality synthetic medical images may support research workflows, but the reported fidelity proxies do not establish clinical safety or diagnostic utility.
method: Compared natural-image initialization with training from scratch, medical pretraining, and reinitialization schemes.
Evaluated pixel- and latent-space diffusion models spanning 131M–952M parameters.
Probed denoiser representations and tested mixed natural–medical image training.
evidence_signal: Across RadImageNet and BraTS, natural-image initialization improved relative gFID by 21–34% in pixel space and 14% in latent space, with gains mirrored by pathology-classification and radiomic-feature evaluations.
watch_item: Results cover two datasets and rely on fidelity proxies; broader generalization and clinical usefulness remain unestablished.
paper_title: From Natural Images to Medical Scans: Transferability of Diffusion Models for Medical Image Generation
